title: Bangladesh, Netherlands sign MoU on circular economy cooperation
content:
The Netherlands and Bangladesh recently signed an MoU in Dhaka on cooperation in circular economy. 
The domains include resource efficiency across the textile value chain, waste reduction, recycling, sustainable production systems and green transition in the textile and apparel sector. 
Such cooperation is essential on the path to graduating from the LDC status, commerce minister Khandaker A Muktadir said.

title: Progress of Tumakuru Node land acquisition in India’s Karnataka smooth
content:
The land acquisition for Tumakuru Node—an industrial manufacturing hub in India’s Karnataka state—has been smoothly progressing, state minister for commerce & industries and infrastructure M B Patil said. 
The project is scheduled for completion in 2027. 
The Tumakuru Node—part of the Bengaluru-Chennai Industrial Corridor—has achieved 30 per cent physical progress and 20 per cent financial progress.

title: India, Bangladesh propose two task forces to boost trade, investment
content:
CII has proposed two joint task forces with Bangladesh on infrastructure and high-tech sectors to turn bilateral trade talks into projects.
Land-port delays, particularly at Benapole, and raw-material movement were flagged as cost issues for cross-border supply chains.
Duty rationalisation for energy-efficient steam technologies could affect textile, RMG and food-processing manufacturers.

title: South India cotton yarn faces headwinds, prices up but demand slow
content:
South India’s cotton yarn market moved in opposite trends; southern mills raised rates by ₹7 per kg, and Tiruppur prices increased by ₹4-5 per kg.
Mumbai yarn prices stayed stable as slow fabric demand hurt sentiment and loom owners were bound to sell below cost.
Gujarat cotton rose by ₹1,000 per candy; Shankar-6 traded at ₹68,900-69,500, and southern mills looked to buy at ₹69,500-70,000.

title: India's polyester buying window could tighten further before festivals
content:
Polyester filament yarn prices diverged across Asia in the week ended August 14, 2026.
India’s DTY 150D/48F closed at ₹139/kg, up 2.21 per cent week on week.
China’s DTY rose 0.53 per cent to CNY 9,450/mt; POY 150D/48F stayed flat at CNY 8,400/mt.
Pakistan gained 2.02 per cent to PKR 202/kg; divergence is narrowing Surat and Bhiwandi’s pre-festive sourcing window.

title: India’s raw silk production edges up in 2025-26
content:
India's raw silk production rose 2.22 per cent YoY to 42,033 tonnes in 2025–26, Central Silk Board statistics show. 
Mulberry silk remained dominant at 32,250 tonnes, as higher-quality bivoltine silk increased 10.52 per cent to 11,229 tonnes. 
Vanya silk declined 2.19 per cent to 9,783 tonnes, while mulberry cultivation area expanded 3.07 per cent to 269,670 hectares.

title: FBCCI calls for Chinese investment to boost Bangladesh exports
content:
FBCCI says Bangladesh-China trade is near $20 billion, but Bangladesh exports to China remain below $1 billion a year. 
The chamber has urged stronger business engagement and joint investment to reduce the deficit.
Chinese investors were asked to examine jute products, food processing, medical devices, pharmaceuticals and renewable energy.

title: What prompted US' Wolverine Worldwide to lift its 2026 forecast?
content:
Wolverine Worldwide reported second-quarter (Q2) revenue of $506.4 million, up 6.8 per cent year on year, led by Merrell and Saucony.
International sales rose 10.9 per cent, while higher US tariffs pressured gross margin.
The company raised its 2026 revenue and earnings outlook, citing continued business momentum and stronger brand performance across markets.
